# Restoration models

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_docs.py from the model cards; do not edit. -->

16 restoration models. Each section says what the model is, whether it may be used commercially and how fast it is; licences and checks are under Details.

Input: one RGB image. Output: the restored (upscaled) image, `model.scale` x the input size, RGB in [0, 1]. `tile=` runs large images in overlapping tiles (as ComfyUI).

Measured on RTX 5060 Ti, torch 2.14.1+cu130; `fastforks bench MODEL --size HxW` measures yours. The summary uses one input, 512x512: kernels time with its speed-up over the faster original run, and kernels peak reserved memory with its ratio to the smaller original one. Where measured (one variant per family), a variant's table also lists portable under `torch.compile` and the fp16 TensorRT engine of portable ([export](../export.md); memory: the engine's device memory + torch's peak). – = not measured.

Other devices: [Apple M1 Pro 16 GB](../devices/apple-m1-pro-16gb.md), [NVIDIA L4](../devices/l4-22gb.md), [NVIDIA L40S](../devices/l40s-44gb.md), [NVIDIA A10](../devices/a10-22gb.md), [NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB](../devices/a100-sxm4-40gb.md), [NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000](../devices/rtx-pro-6000-96gb.md); [across devices](../benchmarks.md#other-devices).

## CodeFormer

CodeFormer (Zhou et al., S-Lab NTU, NeurIPS 2022): restores a degraded face (an aligned 512 x 512 crop) by predicting codes of a learned face codebook; fidelity w trades quality against faithfulness. Non-commercial code and weights (S-Lab License 1.0).

Commercial use: **no** (code: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); weights: LicenseRef-noncommercial).

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `codeformer` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 85.7<br>48.6<br>–<br>30.8<br>16.3 | 959 / 1090<br>512 / 638<br>–<br>407 / 458<br>593 / 642 |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Paper: [Towards Robust Blind Face Restoration with Codebook Lookup Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11253), NeurIPS 2022, 2022-06-22
- Original code: <https://github.com/sczhou/CodeFormer> at `b33cc7d639d6`
- Code licence: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: LicenseRef-noncommercial
- Licence evidence: https://github.com/sczhou/CodeFormer/blob/b33cc7d639d6545bfcccc7e0bc6ae51f24e79c2b/LICENSE ; https://github.com/sczhou/CodeFormer/blob/b33cc7d639d6545bfcccc7e0bc6ae51f24e79c2b/README.md (weights: https://github.com/sczhou/CodeFormer/releases/tag/v0.1.0)
- Training data: Flickr-Faces-HQ (FFHQ, 70k face images) (Paper Sec. 4.1: FFHQ (70 000 faces, resized to 512 x 512) with synthetic degradations (blur, downsampling, noise, JPEG).)
- Options: `fidelity` = 0.5 (0.0 to 1.0; also `fidelity_weight`)
- Kernel libraries: none (not built yet: a VQGAN of 3x3 convolutions with GroupNorm around a 16 x 16 transformer; fp16-accumulate convolutions (`cudnn_hacc`) are the next step)
- Variants: `codeformer`
- Outputs: image
- Input size: any H x W >= 512, padded to a multiple of 32
- Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): `codeformer` 512x512 (0.5 GiB peak allocated, 0.7 reserved)
- `codeformer` 512x512, first call: portable + torch.compile 34 s (cold Inductor cache), TensorRT fp16 65 s (ONNX + engine).
- `codeformer` original 512x512: upstream inference_codeformer.py on the aligned face, float32, w 0.5
- `codeformer` load / first call: original 1.24 s / 0.406 s, portable 0.69 s / 0.228 s
- Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

### Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.002 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.02 and p99 <= 0.25 (absolute error of the output `image`).

| variant | kernels error vs original, mean / p99 | GPU, torch | kernels used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `codeformer` | no kernels backend | - | - |

## DAT

DAT (Chen et al., ICCV 2023): a x4 upscaler for clean (bicubic) images that alternates spatial and channel attention, in three sizes (DAT, DAT-2, DAT-light). Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dat-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile | 9564<br>1565<br>1421<br>1063 | 2443 / 2528<br>2552 / 2624<br>2737 / 2864<br>2552 / 2606 |
| `dat-2-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile | 4880<br>1338<br>1247<br>964 | 2436 / 2518<br>2546 / 2618<br>2730 / 2858<br>2546 / 2598 |
| `dat-light-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile | 2204<br>268<br>268<br>158 | 1606 / 1656<br>1535 / 1552<br>1535 / 1572<br>1385 / 1412 |

### Measured

DIV2K validation HR images and the official bicubic LR images (x4 or x2, the model's scale), one pass without tiles; PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) on the Y channel (BT.601) of the output rounded to uint8, `scale` px border cropped, averaged over the images. Real-ESRGAN is trained for real-world degradations, not bicubic, so its PSNR is low: the numbers compare our modes with the original, not with PSNR-oriented upscalers. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

## HAT

HAT (Chen et al., CVPR 2023): a x4 upscaler mixing window attention, channel attention and overlapping cross-attention: two models for clean (bicubic) images (large and small) and a GAN model for real-world photos. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `hat-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile | 3038<br>1596<br>1445<br>1185 | 5318 / 6106<br>2426 / 2590<br>2610 / 2790<br>1811 / 2750 |
| `hat-s-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile | 2402<br>1072<br>974<br>750 | 5018 / 5644<br>1984 / 2148<br>1985 / 2088<br>2352 / 3068 |
| `real-hat-gan-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile | 3038<br>1597<br>1445<br>1185 | 5318 / 6106<br>2426 / 2610<br>2610 / 2770<br>1811 / 2750 |

## Real-ESRGAN

Real-ESRGAN (Wang et al., Tencent ARC, 2021): upscales real-world photos (x4, x2) and anime images (x4) with an RRDB network trained on synthetic degradations (blur, noise, JPEG); the classic ComfyUI upscaler. BSD-3-Clause code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |

## SPAN

SPAN (Wan et al., NTIRE 2024 efficient SR winner): a small, fast x4 / x2 upscaler for clean (bicubic) images, convolutions with parameter-free attention. Apache-2.0 code and weights.

Commercial use: yes.

| variant | input | backend | time (ms) | peak memory (MiB, allocated / reserved) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `span-x4` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 26.9<br>24.2<br>14.6<br>13.2<br>8.28 | 611 / 648<br>607 / 662<br>487 / 522<br>204 / 222<br>319 / 346 |
| `span-x2` | synthetic (512x512) | original<br>portable<br>kernels<br>portable + torch.compile<br>TensorRT fp16 | 24.6<br>23.5<br>14.9<br>13.2<br>7.98 | 611 / 648<br>607 / 662<br>487 / 522<br>204 / 222<br>243 / 266 |

<details><summary>Details</summary>

- Paper: [Swift Parameter-free Attention Network for Efficient Super-Resolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.12770), CVPRW 2024, 2023-11-21
- Original code: <https://github.com/hongyuanyu/SPAN> at `c77a5917759f`
- Code licence: Apache-2.0 (permissive); files: `LICENSE`
- Weights licence: Apache-2.0
- Licence evidence: https://github.com/hongyuanyu/SPAN/blob/c77a5917759f09e66fbc7124220c5afc5ee221e5/LICENSE.txt ; https://github.com/hongyuanyu/SPAN/blob/c77a5917759f09e66fbc7124220c5afc5ee221e5/README.md
- Training data: DIV2K (NTIRE 2017 super-resolution, 1000 2K images), Flickr2K (2650 2K Flickr images, EDSR) (Paper Sec. 4.1: DF2K (DIV2K + Flickr2K) HR images, bicubic-downsampled.)

- `span-x2` original 512x512: .half() on 1 modules, fp16 inputs; upstream SPAN eval mode, float32, net(lq) clamped

## SwinIR

SwinIR (Liang et al., ICCVW 2021): a Swin Transformer upscaler: x4 / x2 for clean (bicubic) images and x4 for real-world photos (medium and large). Apache-2.0 code and weights.
